question: Citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina have raised the issue of the unacceptable way in which the country’s three official languages are used on the website of the OSCE Mission to BiH. The website gives users the option of choosing between English or Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian (BCS). However, if Croatian is selected, the texts remain in Bosnian, meaning that the ‘C’ option is purely decorative.
This practice violates Article 6 of the Federation’s Constitution, which places all three languages (Bosnian, Croatian and Serbian) on an equal footing.

Given that the European Union contributes more than two thirds of the OSCE’s main budget, and also contributes to additional projects and provides staff and equipment in full support of the organisation in its work for stability, peace and democracy, does the Commission intend to admonish the OSCE Mission to BiH for the noted unacceptable practice of failing to treat the three official languages of Bosnia and Herzegovina equally, and how will it go about this?
answer: The linguistic regime of the website of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) Mission to Bosnia and Herzegovina is a matter that falls outside the remit of the Commission. The Commission funds some regional and bilateral projects implemented by the OSCE across its area of operation under its extra-budgetary contributions. However, the Commission does not directly provide EU funds to the OSCE’s unified budget.
